answer.evidence: The object is a stack of three display tiers. The top tray (rows 0-6) shows red goods inside a yellow tray, which is evidence (d). The first wooden tier has a 3-row top band (rows 9-11) ending in a light front-edge line at row 11, then a 4-row front face (rows 12-15) with a red goods panel. The second tier (rows 17-21) and third tier (rows 23-27) show only a 1-row light lip above a front face with blue and green panels, so they read as front elevations. No side face is drawn. The main top is a thin 3-row band, which is borderline, but the front face is 4 rows or more.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf unit about 13x23 px with a dark brown frame and stacked bands of red, yellow, blue and orange goods. The outline is tinted (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so it is not the black sticker look. It has 10 visible tones per tile and 0% near-flat coverage, which matches the hedge (9) but sits well below the stall (17) and the roofed well (20), the closest merchant and structure references. By eye the frame and goods read as only about 3 steps each, with little grain, no per-item highlights and no wood texture. The coloured bands are close to flat blocks, whereas the stall shows shaded goods, a striped awning with highlights, and grain. It is cleanly drawn but thinner and flatter than the Beodeul standard, and when in doubt it fails.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small shelf unit built from stacked coloured bands inside a dark brown frame. The measured facts are acceptable: 10 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted rather than near-black. By eye the structure is shallow. Each band (red, yellow, orange, blue) reads as roughly 2-3 lightness steps, with little per-item shading, grain or highlight clustering. It lacks the 5-6 step ramps, scalloped awning highlights and goods shaded one by one that the cheese stall and roofed well have, and those two reach 17-20 tones per tile. The tone count is also inflated because the bands use several different hues, not several lightness steps. Next to the stall reference it looks thinner and more like flat colour swatches, so I am failing it on the 'when in doubt' rule.
